A 37-year-old male seeks medical attention for chronic symptoms including fatigue, abdominal
discomfort, diarrhea, and weight loss. His abdominal pain improves after defecation, and he produces
large, malodorous stools. His medical history includes an ACL injury and a previous transfusion
reaction requiring epinephrine. He takes vitamin D and ibuprofen. Recently, he went camping in the
eastern U.S., where he consumed fire-cooked packaged meats and stream water. Vital signs show:
Temperature 98.8°F (37.5°C), BP 120/77 mmHg, pulse 86/min, respirations 10/min, and O2 saturation
98% on room air. Examination reveals ataxia and poor motor control, with normal cardiac and
pulmonary findings. Laboratory results: - Hemoglobin: 9.0 g/dL - Hematocrit: 25% - Haptoglobin: 12
mg/dL - WBC: 7,500/mm^3 (normal differential) - Platelets: 255,000/mm^3 - Na+: 140 mEq/L - Cl-: 102
mEq/L - K+: 5.0 mEq/L - HCO3-: 24 mEq/L - BUN: 24 mg/dL - Glucose: 82 mg/dL - Creatinine: 1.0
mg/dL - Ca2+: 9.0 mg/dL - LDH: 457 U/L - AST: 11 U/L - ALT: 11 U/L Imaging reveals a left tibial stress
fracture. Which diagnostic test would be most appropriate to confirm the underlying condition? Answer
Choices: (A) Serum IgA anti-tissue transglutaminase antibodies (B) Bowel wall biopsy (C) Fecal
calprotectin level (D) Stool culture and ova/parasite examination (E) Stool ELISA (F) Serum B12 level
(G) Anti-Saccharomyces cerevisiae antibodies (ASCA) (H) Upper endoscopy with D2 aspiration (I)
Vitamin E level (J) Hydrogen breath test
 A. Hydrogen breath test
B. Stool culture and ova/parasite examination
C. Serum IgA anti-tissue transglutaminase antibodies
D. Vitamin E level
E. Fecal calprotectin level
F. Upper endoscopy with D2 aspiration
G. Bowel wall biopsy
H. Anti-Saccharomyces cerevisiae antibodies (ASCA)
I. Stool ELISA
J. Serum B12 level
